In GSI, this manifests as calibrated uncertainty bounds around player projections using Tweedie distributions. The engine refusal boundary emerges from comparing these calibrated diagnostics against static thresholds derived from stale branch comparisons. These stale branches contain unique diagnostic methods not present in main or intelligence branches—specifically, the Tweedie ACI and baseline implementations in rescue/intelligence-core-2026-06-28. This suggests a dual failure mode: either the model lacks sufficient calibration (via Tweedie diagnostics), or the engine refuses operation due to exceeding a dynamic refusal boundary. Both primitives form a closed-loop feedback mechanism within GSE’s reasoning architecture, where empirical diagnostics inform state transitions.
